title: Trust Infrastructure Comparison Matrix
status: cross-dossier synthesis; observations and project syntheses separated

rows.trust_object: monetary value, payment reliability and financial-system stability
rows.legitimacy_basis: statute, independence and public monetary mandate
rows.decision_architecture: centralized expert central-bank governance with statutory independence
rows.material_capacity: balance sheet, market operations, payment/settlement functions, data and oversight capability
rows.principal_doors: settlement/access rules, monetary-policy transmission, institutional eligibility
rows.principal_eye: financial-system analysis, statistics and infrastructure oversight
rows.principal_fruit: price/payment/system stability and reliable monetary infrastructure
rows.principal_shadow: counterfactual crises avoided and causal attribution of preventive oversight
rows.mission_drift_risk: synthesis question: whether internal metrics/incentives ever detach from statutory mandate
rows.goodhart_risk: using one stability or profit indicator as proxy for the whole mandate
rows.capability_question: Does the institution increase the wider system's ability to transact and absorb shocks without creating hidden dependency?

rows.trust_object: free, durable and accessible knowledge infrastructure
rows.legitimacy_basis: nonprofit mission plus volunteer/community participation and public openness norms
rows.decision_architecture: central Foundation governance coupled to decentralized volunteer editorial governance
rows.material_capacity: software, servers, legal/privacy support, staff, grants and fundraising
rows.principal_doors: account permissions, community editorial processes, legal requests, technical APIs/access
rows.principal_eye: public edit histories, transparency reporting, community review and governance records
rows.principal_fruit: accessible free knowledge plus contributor/community capacity
rows.principal_shadow: representation gaps, contributor health, AI-mediated consumption and distributed governance effects
rows.mission_drift_risk: central infrastructure growth could theoretically outpace or crowd community capability; requires evidence, not assumption
rows.goodhart_risk: traffic, article count or fundraising becoming substitutes for knowledge quality and community health
rows.capability_question: Does central support leave communities more able to govern, create and preserve knowledge independently?

rows.trust_object: shared long-horizon scientific inquiry and infrastructure
rows.legitimacy_basis: intergovernmental convention, Member State governance and scientific community norms
rows.decision_architecture: Council/committee governance plus expert experiment and programme structures
rows.material_capacity: accelerators, detectors, computing, laboratories, engineering and international funding
rows.principal_doors: membership, experiment participation, facility access, programme approval
rows.principal_eye: scientific review, Council oversight, strategy processes, experiment publication and replication
rows.principal_fruit: knowledge, technical capability, trained people and scientific option value
rows.principal_shadow: future discovery value, long-horizon opportunity cost and distribution of spillovers
rows.mission_drift_risk: large infrastructure programmes may create path dependence; whether this distorts scientific priorities is an empirical question
rows.goodhart_risk: near-term publication/discovery metrics obscuring infrastructure, training and option value
rows.capability_question: Does shared infrastructure expand the scientific capability of the broader community rather than only centralizing it?

rows.trust_object: neutral humanitarian access, protection and assistance
rows.legitimacy_basis: humanitarian principles, international humanitarian law role and field practice
rows.decision_architecture: Assembly/Directorate governance plus field assessment, negotiation and legal expertise
rows.material_capacity: field offices, logistics, medical/water systems, staff, tracing and donor funding
rows.principal_doors: negotiated access to people, places and parties in conflict
rows.principal_eye: field observation, accountability/evaluation, protection data and annual reporting
rows.principal_fruit: protection, access, health, water, tracing and restored capability
rows.principal_shadow: non-random access gaps, confidentiality, denied areas and counterfactual prevention effects
rows.mission_drift_risk: funding concentration and operational constraints create a question about independence; no causal drift claim without evidence
rows.goodhart_risk: counting assistance outputs while missing access quality, dignity, local capability or unserved populations
rows.capability_question: When does relief restore durable local capability rather than only immediate survival?

comparative_revelations: Trust architectures differ in what they ask people to rely on, but all require alignment of mandate, decision quality and executable capacity.
Door design is central in all four cases: settlement, editing/legal access, scientific participation and humanitarian access determine who can use or influence the system.
Shadow differs by domain: prevention counterfactuals, distributed community data, unknown scientific futures and conflict-access missingness are four distinct missingness mechanisms.
Fruit cannot be compared as one KPI across sectors; each requires purpose-specific outcome bundles plus externality/capability checks.
A useful general integrity test is Spirit↔Mind↔Body alignment over time, but any claim of drift must remain entity-specific and evidence-based.
